obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Determination that a Cyber Security Incident compromised or disrupted a medium impact BES Cyber System or its EACMS at the TCC (NERC Glossary definition)
deadline: Within 1 hour after the determination; include functional impact, attack vector, and level of intrusion to the extent known
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - medium impact BES Cyber Systems at the TCC. In the exercise scenario the EACMS were probed but not compromised, so this row was not triggered
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (NERC compliance director; CIP Senior Manager approves determinations)
clock_starts: Determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 attempt to compromise notification
trigger: Determination, using the plan's criteria (R1 Part 1.2.1), that a Cyber Security Incident was an attempt to compromise a medium impact BES Cyber System or its EACMS
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - exercise scenario: scans and login attempts against the TCC Electronic Access Point (an EACMS) from the compromised DOP path
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (NERC compliance director; CIP Senior Manager approves determinations)
clock_starts: Determination of an attempt to compromise

trigger: New or changed information about a reported incident or attempt
deadline: Within 7 calendar days of determining new or changed information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (NERC compliance director; CIP Senior Manager approves determinations)

obligation: E-ISAC notice of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident at a low impact asset
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that compromised or disrupted a low impact BES Cyber System at one of the 74 transmission substations
deadline: CIP-003-9 sets no fixed time; notification follows the determination unless prohibited by law. Group target: within 1 hour of the determination (POL-03 4.5)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - exercise scenario: the gateway login attempts failed, so the incident was determined not Reportable; the determination is recorded
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (NERC compliance director; CIP Senior Manager approves determinations)
clock_starts: Determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident

citation: Form DOE-417 criteria 2 and 3; Federal Energy Administration Act of 1974 sec. 13(b) (Pub. L. 93-275); OMB 1901-0288
trigger: Criterion 2: a Reportable Cyber Security Incident. Criterion 3: a cyber event that is not a Reportable Cyber Security Incident but causes interruptions of electrical system operations
deadline: Within 1 hour of the incident (telephone notice to the DOE Emergency Operations Center is acceptable when operations are critical, followed by the form)
notify: DOE (DOE-417 online system); the form can be shared with NERC, the E-ISAC, and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - exercise scenario: unauthorized commands opened 6 feeders (criterion 3)
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (DCC shift supervisor starts; NERC compliance director files)

trigger: Criterion 11: a cyber event that could potentially affect electric power system adequacy or reliability. Criterion 12: loss of electric service to more than 50,000 customers for 1 hour or more
deadline: Within 6 hours of the incident if no Emergency Alert criterion applies
applies_at_this_tier: Covered by the Emergency Alert in the exercise (38,000 customers for about 70 minutes does not meet criterion 12)

trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that was an attempt to compromise high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems or their EACMS
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination, if no earlier criterion applies; check box 14 on the Emergency Alert when both apply
notify: DOE; can satisfy CIP-008 reporting if shared with the E-ISAC and CISA through the form
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the TCC EAP probing; reported on the same form as criterion 3

trigger: Significant new information; every filed report
deadline: Update when significant information becomes available; final report (updated Schedule 1 and all of Schedule 2) within 72 hours of the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: NERC EOP-004-4 R2 and Attachment 1 (TO, TOP, DP events)
trigger: For example: uncontrolled loss of firm load of 300 MW or more for 15 minutes or more (peak demand of 3,000 MW or more); damage or destruction of its Facility from actual or suspected intentional human action; complete loss of monitoring or control at its staffed BES control center for 30 continuous minutes or more
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognizing that a threshold was met or the end of the next business day (4 p.m. local time)
notify: NERC (systemawareness@nerc.net) and the parties in the Operating Plan; a DOE-417 form may be used as the report
applies_at_this_tier: Checked: not met in the exercise (about 70 MW interrupted; no damage; TCC monitoring unaffected)
clock_starts: Recognition that a threshold was met

obligation: Operational notices to the RC, BA, and neighboring TOPs
citation: Interconnection and operating agreements; RC directives
trigger: Any event that affects or could affect BES Facilities, transmission substations, or load served from the BES
deadline: Immediately by phone from the TCC
notify: Reliability Coordinator; Balancing Authority; neighboring TOPs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and operational, not a cyber reporting rule

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
trigger: Any intrusion into OT in any division
deadline: As soon as practicable (group target: same day)
notify: CISA (report.cisa.gov or CISA Central); FBI field office
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports response help and OFAC mitigation

obligation: Client notice of a vendor-identified incident
citation: Client contracts (CIP-013-2 Part 1.2.1 terms in 37 contracts)
trigger: An incident at Engineering Services related to products or services it provides that poses cyber security risk to the client (for example, theft of the client's BCSI or misuse of an engineer's access)
deadline: Per contract: 24 hours (9 contracts), 48 hours (11), or 72 hours (17) after Engineering Services identifies the incident
notify: Each affected client's security contact (from the client notice register)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - exercise scenario: files from 3 client projects downloaded with the engineer's session, including one client's substation BCSI
clock_starts: Identification of the incident by Engineering Services (the group SOC counts)

obligation: Client notice that access should be revoked
trigger: An engineer's remote or on-site access to a client should end (for example, a compromised account)
deadline: Per contract: 1 to 3 business days; group target the same day
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the phished engineer holds access at 2 external clients

obligation: Engineering Services notice to the Electric Utility (affiliate as vendor)
citation: POL-01 4.8; intercompany agreement (no notice term yet, POAM-011)
trigger: Incident at Engineering Services affecting Electric Utility systems or BCSI
deadline: Immediately on the group bridge (group rule)
notify: Electric Utility NERC compliance director and CIP Senior Manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the Electric Utility TCC BCSI folder on SYS-S1 was among the files accessed
notifying_entity: Engineering Services security and compliance lead

trigger: A cyber event at Gas Production that puts contracted deliveries at risk
deadline: As the contract requires (operational notice the same gas day)
applies_at_this_tier: Checked: no delivery impact in the exercise (POC logins failed)
notifying_entity: Gas Production vice president of marketing

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated pipeline
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification
notify: CISA Central; CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - Gas Production operates no pipeline and has no TSA notice (P03)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Identification of covered telecommunications equipment or services during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Only if found while performing Engineering Services federal civilian contracts; not expected in this scenario

trigger: Identification of a covered article (Kaspersky Lab products) during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Only if found while performing federal contracts; not expected

trigger: Identification of a covered article subject to a FASCSA order
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the clause is not in current contracts; recheck in new awards

trigger: Determination that a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the holding company is an SEC registrant; the disclosure committee decides materiality

trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe risk management, strategy, and governance; consider lessons from the incident

citation: State breach notification statutes; worked example Fla. Stat. 501.171(4)
trigger: Breach of personal information (for example, name with SSN, or a user name with password) of residents
deadline: Varies by state; Florida: no later than 30 days after determination (15-day extension for good cause applies only to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Checked: no personal information found in the files taken in the exercise; recheck when forensics completes

trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more Florida residents (other states set their own thresholds)
deadline: Florida: no later than 30 days after determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs; other states' regulators as their laws require
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the individual threshold is met

trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals are notified

obligation: Vendor breach notice to the group (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example, the CIS or AMI vendor) discovers a breach of group personal information
deadline: Within 10 days after determination; contracts should require faster notice
applies_at_this_tier: Track in vendor contracts; not triggered in the exercise

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; no demand in the exercise

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before hiring response vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (proposed only)

trigger: Cyber attack affecting a power reactor licensee's digital assets
deadline: 1 hour, 4 hours, or 8 hours depending on the event
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no NRC reactor license
